propositions: Five tests carry docstrings promising contracts they never check; each has been verified by reading both test body and code under test to contain vacuous or reimplemented assertions that will not fail if the property regresses.

Tests 1, 3, 4, and 5 omit the actual assertion the docstring names; test 2 reimplements an audit predicate inline instead of calling the shared helper, so breaking the helper leaves the teeth test green.

The PAT-repr test constructs a transport that never receives a credential, so no credential can leak into repr; the credentials used elsewhere in the module are fed to a different API and never reach the transport under test.
The pagination-guard teeth test re-implements the AST walk inline rather than calling _search_issues_calls_taking_the_default(), which means if that predicate regresses the teeth stay buried.

The assignee-validation test asserts only hasattr(...), which is already asserted verbatim by the parametrized presence test in the same file; nothing asserts the return value is a username string for DC or accountId for Cloud.

The rate-limit sweep asserts total <= 1, which is satisfied by 0 client calls (meaning the 429 branch was never reached); the blanket pytest.raises(Exception) also overstates what the type assertion covers.
